LESSON: ANGLES

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade six
Subject: MATHEMATICS
Strand: Geometry
Topic 3.2: Angles
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 6

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Angles, part of Geometry in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade six MATHEMATICS.

Key inquiry question: How are angles used in day to day life?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Angles together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
50

• Communication and Collaboration: The learner develops speaking and listening skills and also embrace teamwork as

they work in groups to identify angles on a straight line.

Values:
• Unity: The learner collaborates with others as they compare sizes of angles.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

• Learner Support Programme: The learner enhances peer education and mentorship to support one another in

establishing the sum of angles in a triangle and rectangles from different objects in the environment.

Links to other Learning Areas:
• Creative Arts: The learner measures and draws different angles from a straight line.

Suggested Learning Resources:

Clay, plasticine/modeling clay, paper cut outs, pair of scissors, tactile angles, models of angles, toys, geometrical shapes

models of different angles, reference materials in Braille and in appropriate print
